headline: High risk of prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors when Cognee feeds into LangGraph’s writable, networked orchestration defaults.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cognee ingests documents, support history, and workflows, while LangGraph can read files and run browser/subprocess tools with developer-wired edges. That creates a default pathway where Cognee content can be passed into LangGraph as trusted input. No shared channel is explicit, so I do not escalate to high.
conditions: IF Cognee outputs are routed into LangGraph nodes without provenance checks
IF LangGraph tools parse Cognee-generated text as instructions
mitigations: Add a provenance tag to every Cognee output before passing it onward
Insert a prompt-injection filter on all Cognee-to-LangGraph inputs
Restrict LangGraph nodes to structured JSON only
Disable browser/tool nodes for untrusted Cognee content
requires-engineering: add per-hop content signing and verification

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cognee touches personal data, finance data, support history, and documents. LangGraph has broad network egress and can read/write application files, so the pair can move sensitive data from Cognee into external model providers or tools by default. The blast radius includes exfiltration and compliance breach, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF Cognee data is forwarded into LangGraph tool calls or model-provider prompts
IF LangGraph is configured with access to the same sensitive workspace
mitigations: Limit LangGraph inputs to redacted fields only
Block network egress for workflows handling personal or finance data
Separate Cognee and LangGraph workspaces
Review tool allowlists for any external API calls
requires-engineering: add DLP scanning before every outbound call

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cognee supports multiple instances with session memory and tenant isolation, while LangGraph uses shared checkpointer state and writable filesystem-backed application files. Overlap on mutable state can cause write contention or state corruption even without git access. The conflict is plausible in default orchestration setups, so medium fits.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same checkpointer or application directory
IF multiple LangGraph invocations share the same persistent store
mitigations: Assign separate storage namespaces per agent
Serialize writes to shared state
Use per-tenant checkpointer keys
Audit filesystem paths for overlap
requires-engineering: add locking around shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cognee produces decisions, workflows, schema structures, and successful implementations, and LangGraph is a stateful orchestration layer that can execute developer-defined tools. If LangGraph treats Cognee output as authoritative, errors can cascade into automated actions or downstream tool calls. The default orchestration pattern makes this dangerous.
conditions: IF LangGraph nodes consume Cognee output without verification
IF downstream nodes act on Cognee-derived facts or decisions
mitigations: Insert a human review step before action-taking nodes
Require schema validation on Cognee outputs
Add confidence thresholds before execution
Log and diff Cognee claims against source data
requires-engineering: implement verification gates between nodes

E_compliance.rationale: Cognee explicitly touches personal data and finance data, while LangGraph handles model-provider API keys and broad network egress. That combination can create residency, retention, or disclosure mismatches when regulated data is routed through LangGraph-managed calls. The profiles do not prove a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF regulated personal or finance data is sent through LangGraph-managed model-provider calls
IF retention or residency policies differ between Cognee storage and LangGraph tool logs
mitigations: Classify regulated fields before orchestration
Exclude regulated data from external model prompts
Set retention limits on LangGraph logs
Document data-flow boundaries for compliance review
requires-engineering: add residency-aware routing and audit trails
